Implementation Plan

The plan is ready. Planning is on `orchestrator/project-7490` at `3b3fcce5de667cdef57d8f9f5c82de103927dc99`, which matches the integration branch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md
Scope-mode justification: The issue names exactly two files: delete one source doc and add to the existing report. The report already records each processed doc the same way (a list entry under `## Processed source docs (N)` plus a `### <doc>` section with `Processed:` and verdict bullets). This change follows that pattern and adds no code, script or workflow. All four sibling changes are already on this branch, so every `applied` verdict can be recorded as `applied` and none has to become `rejected`. A broader scope would break the issue's "stay inside the two files listed" rule.

## Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- No new script, supervisor, scheduler entry or database work.
- No scheduler or PR-push entry point is touched. This is a one-time report closeout in the orchestrator project's final PR.
- No `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry is needed.

- `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` (additions only)

## Data structures affected
None. The only "structure" is the report's Markdown layout: one heading count, one list entry, and one new section at the end.

## API or interface changes
None.

## Decisions
### D1 — Record sibling verdicts as applied
- Chosen: record the three applied and one applied-in-part verdicts as the issue lists them, because each sibling's script change and changelog fragment are on `orchestrator/project-7490`.
- Alternatives considered: the issue's fallback of `rejected` with "not merged in this project".
- Why: the greps above confirm all four siblings are on the branch, so the fallback does not apply.

### D2 — No changelog fragment
- Chosen: add no `changelog.d/` fragment.
- Alternatives considered: a fragment describing the report closeout.
- Why: the issue says a report-only change needs no fragment unless CLAUDE.md §20 requires one. Earlier closeouts of this report (e.g. 2026-09-20) shipped without their own fragment, and the issue's "two files only" rule forbids adding a third file.

### D3 — Append the new section at the end of the file
- Chosen: add the new section after the existing 2026-09-20 section, at end of file.
- Alternatives considered: insert it in date order somewhere earlier.
- Why: the issue asks for end-of-file and additions only. Appending gives the smallest diff and cannot reflow earlier sections.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: none touched. No code, workflow, credential or GitHub API surface changes.
- The deleted doc is not read, so its untrusted content never reaches the edit.
- PR body and commits must say `Refs #7490` and must not use close/fix/resolve forms against the tracking issue. Run `scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py` on the composed body; a non-zero exit means `BLOCKED:` (§21).
- Abuse cases: none. The report is documentation only, and no automation parses its verdicts.

## Risks and edge cases
- Deleting or touching other `analysis/` files by accident. Mitigation: confirm with `git diff --stat` that only the two listed paths change.
- The count of 121 assumes the list really has 120 entries now. The implementer may count list entries between line 5 and the next heading. If the real count differs from the heading, still use heading + 1 as the issue says, and note the mismatch in the PR body.
- The date drifts if implementation runs after 2026-10-16 UTC. Use the actual UTC date at write time.
- The file must keep its trailing newline.
- The agents.md fragment rule (§25) does not apply; agents.md is not touched.

## Testing considerations
- No code tests are needed.
- Check `git diff --stat`: one deletion and one file with additions only.
- In `git diff analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`, the only removed line should be the old `(120)` heading.
- Optionally run `python3 tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py`; it is unaffected.
- No test is known to read the report's `Processed source docs` count or the presence of `analysis/` files. CI runs the `lint-plan-archival.yml` lint on PRs and should pass because no plan doc is touched.

## Pre-execution self-check
- The answers were interpreted as the orchestrator's auto-answer; there were no clarification questions.
- Scope is the two files named in the issue.
- All four sibling dependencies were checked on the branch and are present.
- There is no integration-branch mismatch.
- No `BLOCKED` inputs.
